newsitem.title: USA: Entergy Arkansas 1 nuke resumes full power.
newsitem.headline: Entergy Arkansas 1 nuke resumes full power.

text.p: Entergy Corp's 836 megawatt (MW) Arkansas Nuclear unit 1 has resumed full power after operating at a reduced level since tornadoes struck the area earlier this month, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Tuesday in its status report.

The unit, in Russellville, Ark., has been hovering between 50 and 80 percent power over the last two weeks following the storms that knocked out five 500 kilovolt (kv) lines as well as several other smaller transmission lines.
The adjacent unit 2, with a generating capacity of 858 MW, was operating at 73 percent power early Tuesday morning for repairs to the main feedwater pump control system, the NRC report stated.
Last week, the company said three of the 500 kv lines were still out of service. The company was not immediately available to update the status of its operations.

New Orleans-based Entergy maintains about 119,000 miles of transmission and distribution lines in its service territory, which covers parts of Louisiana, Arkansas, Mississippi and eastern Texas. It serves about 611,000 customers.
